The inclusion of digital signage and library management systems will streamline access to both physical and electronic materials, allowing for a seamless experience.
Enhanced Student and Faculty Engagement:

The library will offer a range of academic services, such as research assistance, academic workshops, and tutoring programs. The space will encourage collaborative learning with the availability of group study rooms, presentation areas, and a section dedicated to faculty resources.
The goal is to increase student and faculty participation in library activities, fostering an environment where learning can thrive both independently and collectively.
Sustainability and Modern Technology:

column8:
The National Child Development Center (NCDC) is the community-based flagship program of the ECCD Council. It is the ground level venue of the implementation of ECCD programs and services, particularly the Early Learning Program and the Family Support Program.

The Center aims to (1) introduce best practices of the integrated early childhood care and development services to children below five (5) years old; (2) serve as a laboratory for conducting research and innovations about ECCD that will promote the continuing education and/or professionalization of ECCD service providers; and (3) become the resource center for the community to enhance parenting skills and capabilities. 

The Center is envisioned to enrich community engagement in early childhood education. It also serves as a convergence point for concerted efforts related to early childhood care and development. It is also a repository of related and appropriate data and documents on continuing ECCD programs and services provided to the community.

column4: Summer Institute for Teachers
column6: Human Resource Development for Personnel in Schools and Learning Centers
column8:
Many Junior High School teachers in the Philippines are assigned to teach subjects outside their area of specialization, particularly in Mathematics, Science, and English—subjects that require strong content mastery. This misalignment contributes to persistent learning gaps, as reflected in the 2022 PISA results where Filipino students continued to rank among the lowest globally in reading, mathematics, and science, with no significant improvement since 2018.

Despite existing DepEd policies aimed at minimizing out-of-field teaching, implementation challenges remain. Recent evidence underscores the severity of the issue, with the EDCOM 2 Report (January 2025) revealing that 62% of high school teachers are teaching subjects outside their college specialization, affecting instructional quality and learner outcomes.

To address this, DepEd MIMAROPA, through HRDD-NEAP, will collaborate with Teacher Education Institutions (TEIs) in the region to help bridge teachers’ competency gaps. Through partnerships and possible CSR support, TEIs will offer short-term summer courses in English, Mathematics, and Science to enhance teachers’ subject mastery and pedagogical skills, ultimately improving the quality of basic education for MIMAROPAn learners.
